question: A patient with an undiagnosed chronic cough is admitted to your ward. What precautions should you use first?

options.A: Standard Precautions
options.B: Strict reverse isolation
options.C: Contact Precautions only
options.D: No precautions until lab results return

explanation: Well done! Always start with Standard Precautions for every new admission until specific lab results or doctor's orders guide you otherwise.

question: What do we call the unwritten rules and expected behaviors in a community?

options.A: Boundaries
options.B: Statutes
options.C: Norms
options.D: Values

explanation: Norms are simply the everyday social habits and acceptable behaviors shared by a cultural group.

question: What are the two opposite ends of the Illness-Wellness Continuum?

options.A: Physical weakness and mental strength
options.B: Acute infection and chronic disability
options.C: Hospital admission and complete recovery
options.D: Premature death and high-level wellness

explanation: The continuum ranges from death on the left to optimal wellness on the right. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T3#GNS112_U1_T3_h2)

question: Which cells in the pancreas release insulin to lower your blood sugar after a meal?

options.A: Alpha cells
options.B: Delta cells
options.C: Acinar cells
options.D: Beta cells

explanation: Pancreatic beta cells are your body's sugar sweepers—they release insulin to help cells soak up glucose after you eat.

question: When moving an injured person, what is the most important goal to keep in mind?

options.A: Reaching the nearest hospital in the shortest possible time
options.B: Ensuring the patient's family members can ride along
options.C: Clearing the emergency scene before law enforcement arrives
options.D: Moving the patient safely without causing further injury

explanation: You've got this! Safety and protecting the patient from extra harm always come first, even before rushing to the hospital. Great nursing instincts!

question: What is one effective strategy to ensure two-way communication in a referral system?

options.A: Banning clients from ever returning to their original health post
options.B: Using standardized feedback forms sent back by the receiving facility
options.C: Destroying all medical records once a client leaves the primary clinic
options.D: Stopping all phone calls between hospitals and primary centers

explanation: Two-way feedback forms allow receiving hospitals to report back to the referring nurse on the client's outcome. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h8)

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should check when a patient arrives in the recovery room?

options.A: Maintaining a patent airway and stable vital signs
options.B: Encouraging the patient to walk around the ward
options.C: Serving a full meal to restore energy levels
options.D: Discharging the patient home within one hour

explanation: As soon as a patient comes out of surgery, checking that they are breathing well (patent airway) and that their vitals are stable is always priority number one.

question: What does a cardiotocograph (CTG) machine monitor continuously during labour?

options.A: Maternal core temperature and blood sugar
options.B: Amount of amniotic fluid and bladder volume
options.C: Cervical dilation and pelvic bone width
options.D: Foetal heart rate and uterine contractions

explanation: A CTG machine tracks the baby's heartbeat on one channel and the mother's labour contractions on the other channel simultaneously. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T003#GNS226_U4_T003_h4)

question: Apart from bedside clinical work, what is a key role for a community health nurse?

options.A: Purchasing medical equipment for tertiary teaching hospitals
options.B: Financing the construction of primary healthcare centers
options.C: Acting as an educator and facilitator for health programs
options.D: Drafting national health policies in the federal ministry

explanation: You nailed it! Community nurses spend a lot of time teaching families, running workshops, and helping communities organize their own health activities.

question: What is the main job of the Peripheral Nervous System (PNS)?

options.A: To act as communication lines linking the body to the CNS
options.B: To process and integrate complex memories
options.C: To produce cerebrospinal fluid for the brain
options.D: To directly control hormonal release in the pituitary gland

explanation: The PNS acts like telephone wires, carrying messages back and forth between your body and the central control unit. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T2#GNS211_U3_T2_h2)

question: How has modern surgery for primary bone tumors changed over the years?

options.A: Amputations are performed immediately without trying chemotherapy first
options.B: Radiation is now the sole treatment used for all bone cancers
options.C: Limb-salvage procedures have largely replaced routine amputations
options.D: Surgeries are now completely avoided in favor of long-term antibiotics

explanation: Thanks to awesome tech and medical advances, doctors can often remove just the diseased bone and reconstruct the limb instead of doing an amputation.

question: In Dorothea Orem's theory, what exactly does a 'self-care deficit' mean?

options.A: The hospital has run out of supplies needed for patient hygiene
options.B: The doctor has forbidden the patient from eating solid foods
options.C: The patient's need for self-care is greater than their ability to do it
options.D: The nurse refuses to help the patient walk around the ward

explanation: You nailed it. A self-care deficit simply happens when the care a person needs is higher than what they are currently able to pull off by themselves.

question: A study tests a stress-relief program for nurses in a busy city hospital. What is a great recommendation for future research?

options.A: Firing all city hospital nurses who reported high stress levels
options.B: Replacing human nurses with automated computer terminals
options.C: Testing if the same program works effectively in rural clinics
options.D: Stopping all future research on nurse mental health

explanation: Brilliant! Testing the same idea in a different setting helps us see if it works for nurses everywhere, not just in the city.

question: Why can taking too many fat-soluble vitamins become dangerous?

options.A: All vitamins contain high levels of dangerous dietary sodium
options.B: Excess vitamins immediately turn into stored body fat
options.C: High vitamin levels completely stop normal digestion
options.D: Fat-soluble vitamins can accumulate in the body and cause toxicity

explanation: Unlike water-soluble vitamins that wash right out, fat-soluble ones get stored in body tissues and can build up to harmful levels.

question: A patient is rescued from a motorcycle crash with suspected spinal cord damage. What is the safest immediate action?

options.A: Encourage the patient to stand up and walk quickly
options.B: Twist the neck sideways to check for flexibility
options.C: Drag the victim rapidly by the arms to the clinic
options.D: Avoid unnecessary movement to protect the spine

explanation: Carelessly moving someone with a potential spinal injury can cause permanent paralysis. Always keep them still and protect the spine!

question: Which friendly bacteria is most commonly found keeping a healthy reproductive-age vagina happy and protected?

options.A: Staphylococcus
options.B: Escherichia coli
options.C: Streptococcus
options.D: Lactobacillus

explanation: Lactobacillus is our hero bug here! It's the dominant, protective bacterium that keeps the vaginal environment healthy and balanced. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h1)

question: What is the correct way to fix a writing mistake on a paper patient chart?

options.A: Scratch the incorrect word out completely until it is totally unreadable.
options.B: Apply liquid correction fluid over the mistake and write neatly on top.
options.C: Rip the entire page out of the treatment book and start a fresh one.
options.D: Draw a single line through the error, write mistaken entry, and sign it.

explanation: You got it! A single neat line shows transparency. Never use Tipp-Ex or scribble words out completely—hiding mistakes looks like tampering.

question: How do micronutrients differ from macronutrients?

options.A: Micronutrients provide twice as many calories per gram as macronutrients
options.B: Micronutrients are only necessary during times of severe physical illness
options.C: Micronutrients are needed in much smaller amounts and do not directly provide energy
options.D: Micronutrients are manufactured inside the human liver rather than eaten

explanation: Vitamins and minerals (micronutrients) are like tiny sparks that help body processes run smoothly, even though they don't give direct fuel like carbs do.

question: What key lifestyle advice should nurses give to help prevent osteoporosis in postmenopausal women?

options.A: Avoiding exposure to natural sunlight entirely
options.B: Following a strictly low-protein liquid diet
options.C: Restricting all forms of physical activity
options.D: Engaging in regular weight-bearing exercises

explanation: Activities like walking, jogging, or dancing put gentle pressure on bones, signaling them to stay strong and dense!

question: Where are the ureters positioned in the tummy area?

options.A: Subcutaneous position just beneath the skin
options.B: Medial position inside the peritoneal cavity
options.C: Intraperitoneal position floating near the liver
options.D: Retroperitoneal position along the posterior wall

explanation: Great try! They sit outside the main tummy cavity, running quietly down the back wall behind the peritoneum.

question: How should your team view a test of change that doesn't work out as planned?

options.A: As an emergency that must be reported to the medical board
options.B: As a personal failure of the nursing supervisor on duty
options.C: As proof that quality improvement initiatives never work
options.D: As useful learning data that highlights workflow barriers

explanation: A failed test isn't a bad thing—it's actually a win because it shows you a hidden flaw in the system *before* it can harm a patient!

question: How does health education during antenatal clinics directly help an expectant mother?

options.A: It removes the need for physical examinations by the doctor
options.B: It guarantees that her baby will sleep through the night
options.C: It builds her confidence and encourages positive health behaviors
options.D: It completely stops her from ever experiencing physical fatigue

explanation: Spot on! Knowledge gives mums confidence, calms their fears, and guides them to take great care of themselves and their growing baby.

question: A post-surgical patient cannot pass urine and you suspect they are retaining urine. What is the best bedside tool to check?

options.A: A leg blood flow Doppler
options.B: A portable bladder ultrasound scanner
options.C: A standard chest X-ray
options.D: A full abdominal CT scan

explanation: A portable bladder scanner is quick, non-invasive, and tells you right away how much urine is trapped in the bladder.

question: An item touches a patient's unbroken skin during a routine check-up. According to Spaulding's rules, what level of processing does it need?

options.A: Low-level disinfection
options.B: No processing is required
options.C: Sterilization
options.D: High-level disinfection

explanation: Items that only touch intact skin are non-critical and just need basic low-level disinfection between patients. Simple and straightforward!

question: Why are single-dose deworming treatments not enough on their own without better sanitation?

options.A: Environmental heat instantly neutralizes the therapeutic effect of drugs
options.B: Medicines only kill female worms and leave male worms untouched
options.C: Patients are quickly reinfected from contaminated soil and water sources
options.D: Adult worms immediately mutate to become immune to all known drugs

explanation: Medications clear out the worms you have, but without clean water and toilets, people just pick up new parasites from their surroundings right away.

question: How does a 'just culture' handle a mistake made by a healthcare worker?

options.A: It ignores all mistakes made by senior medical staff
options.B: It fires any nurse involved in an incident immediately
options.C: It assumes that nurses never make unintentional mistakes
options.D: It balances individual accountability with a close look at faulty systems

explanation: You nailed it! A just culture is fair: it separates honest human errors from reckless behavior while fixing the underlying system.

question: What is the main goal of a rehabilitation hospital?

options.A: Restoring lost function and maximizing independence
options.B: Treating acute infectious disease outbreaks
options.C: Stabilizing immediate life-threatening organ failure
options.D: Providing long-term terminal palliative care

explanation: You got this! Rehab hospitals help patients rebuild their strength and everyday skills after major life changes, rather than managing sudden medical emergencies.

question: What does a healthy healing wound bed look like when it's doing well?

options.A: Black and hard
options.B: Yellow and stringy
options.C: Bright red and moist
options.D: Pale white and dry

explanation: You're doing great! Healthy healing tissue (granulation tissue) is packed with fresh blood vessels, giving it a bright red, shiny, and moist look that shows healing is well underway.

question: Why does the physical form of a medication matter so much to a nurse?

options.A: It decides the exact colour the patient will see
options.B: It dictates the correct and safe route of administration
options.C: It guarantees that side effects will never occur
options.D: It proves whether the drug is synthetic or plant-based

explanation: The physical form of a drug determines how it must safely enter the body, such as by mouth, injection, or skin application. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T7#GNS125_U2_T7_h1)

question: How does engaging in research impact a nurse's daily confidence and independence in practice?

options.A: It empowers nurses to make independent, evidence-backed care decisions
options.B: It restricts nurses to performing only basic hygiene tasks
options.C: It forces nurses to ask doctors for permission before speaking
options.D: It stops nurses from collaborating with other health workers

explanation: Exactly! When you know the 'why' behind your care from research, you walk onto the ward with real professional confidence.

question: During a physical exam for a patient with testicular torsion, which reflex is usually missing?

options.A: Cremasteric reflex
options.B: Patellar reflex
options.C: Gag reflex
options.D: Babinski reflex

explanation: Correct! Normally, stroking the inner thigh makes the testicle rise (cremasteric reflex). In torsion, that reflex is completely absent.

question: Which nutritional deficiency is most common in adolescent girls who have heavy periods and poor diets?

options.A: Beriberi and Thiamine deficiency
options.B: Iron-deficiency anemia
options.C: Scurvy and Vitamin C deficiency
options.D: Rickets and Vitamin D deficiency

explanation: Monthly blood loss plus meals lacking in iron easily leads to anemia. It's why adolescent girls often look pale or feel constantly tired, and why nutritional education is so crucial!

question: How is nursing counselling different from a standard health interview?

options.A: Counselling focuses on emotional support and coping
options.B: Counselling relies exclusively on closed-ended questions
options.C: Counselling replaces all physical health assessments
options.D: Counselling is only performed by hospital chaplains

explanation: Great thinking! While an interview gathers facts, counselling helps patients process feelings and handle health challenges.

question: Why is visiting a patient's home so helpful for disease management?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for any medications.
options.B: It guarantees that the patient will never need a hospital visit.
options.C: It allows nurses to observe real-world habits and living conditions.
options.D: It places the entire workload on family members instead.

explanation: You get a true picture when you see where patients actually live! Home care lets you spot daily habits and environmental factors that directly affect their health.

question: How often should you remind families to change the batteries in their smoke alarms?

options.A: Every ten years
options.B: At least once a year
options.C: Only when the fire department visits
options.D: Every two weeks

explanation: Fresh batteries save lives! Changing them at least once a year ensures the smoke detector will actually sound when an emergency happens.

question: Why do patients still need supportive care (like IV fluids and oxygen) even after getting an antidote?

options.A: Antidotes usually worsen the patient's baseline vital signs
options.B: Supportive care keeps the patient stable while the body handles the toxin
options.C: Supportive care replaces the need for any toxicological screening
options.D: Antidotes are completely ineffective without continuous intravenous fluids

explanation: Antidotes are amazing, but they aren't instant magic. Supportive care keeps the patient breathing and stable while the antidote and the body do the heavy lifting to clear the poison.

question: What is the primary hormonal cause of insulin resistance during the second and third trimesters of pregnancy?

options.A: Human placental lactogen
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Follicle stimulating hormone
options.D: Thyroid stimulating hormone

explanation: Placental hormones like human placental lactogen actively block maternal insulin to keep enough glucose in the blood for the growing baby. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T006#GNS226_U4_T006_h1)

question: What actually happens during a drug interaction?

options.A: The normal clearance of a drug through the kidneys
options.B: The physical breakdown of a pill inside the packaging
options.C: An allergic reaction caused by a single medication
options.D: A change in how a drug works because of another substance

explanation: Think of it like mixing ingredients in cooking: a drug interaction happens when another drug, food, or herb changes how your medicine behaves in the body. You've got this!

question: A patient with a wound infected by a multi-drug resistant organism needs which type of precaution?

options.A: Respiratory isolation
options.B: Protective isolation
options.C: Contact isolation
options.D: Airborne isolation

explanation: Resistant germs in open wounds are typically passed through physical touch, making contact isolation necessary. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h3)

question: You are getting ready to hang a unit of blood and notice your patient has a mild fever. What is your best first step?

options.A: Administer ice packs to reduce the temperature and infuse quickly
options.B: Report the fever to the physician before starting the transfusion
options.C: Cancel the transfusion entirely without notifying the doctor
options.D: Proceed with the transfusion and give paracetamol afterward

explanation: Always loop the doctor in! Since fever is also a top sign of a transfusion reaction, we need a baseline check so we don't confuse a pre-existing fever with a reaction later.

question: What is the best position for transporting an unconscious patient who is still breathing and has a pulse?

options.A: High Fowler's position
options.B: Prone position
options.C: Recovery position
options.D: Trendelenburg position

explanation: Brilliant! Placing them on their side (recovery position) keeps the tongue from blocking the airway and lets any fluids drain safely.

question: What is the best immediate physical step to help reduce swelling right after a fresh injury?

options.A: Using a heating pad
options.B: Applying a cold pack
options.C: Placing a warm moist towel
options.D: Giving a deep tissue massage

explanation: Great clinical instinct! Cold constricts blood vessels, which slows down fluid pooling into the area and helps numb the sharp pain right away.

question: What is the minimum head-of-bed elevation for a patient on continuous tube feeding?

options.A: 30 to 45 degrees
options.B: 10 to 15 degrees
options.C: Flat on the back
options.D: 60 to 90 degrees

explanation: Spot on! Keeping the head of the bed raised prevents the formula from flowing backward into the lungs.

question: Why are human reservoirs (like people carrying a germ) harder to track than stationary things like soil?

options.A: Environmental spores cannot be detected by modern laboratory testing
options.B: Infected humans can move freely and spread pathogens before showing symptoms
options.C: Human carriers are completely immune to all forms of standard medical treatment
options.D: Soil bacteria can replicate much faster than any human viral pathogen

explanation: Unlike a patch of soil, people walk around, travel, and mingle—often feeling completely fine while carrying germs. That's what makes human carriers so tricky to spot!

question: What serious heart condition can develop over time from chronic, untreated upper airway obstruction?

options.A: Aortic aneurysm
options.B: Cor pulmonale
options.C: Infective endocarditis
options.D: Mitral valve prolapse

explanation: When blocked airways starve the body of oxygen long-term, blood pressure in the lungs shoots up. This forces the right side of the heart to work overtime until it gets tired and fails (cor pulmonale). You've finished this set—take a bow!

question: What is your main job as a health worker when an unexpected pregnancy emergency happens in the community?

options.A: Provide first-line stabilization and arrange quick transport
options.B: Wait for the patient to reach a specialist hospital
options.C: Prescribe long-term maintenance medications
options.D: Perform immediate major surgery in the village

explanation: You've got this! Since village clinics don't have operating theatres, your primary duty is to stabilize the mother and get her safely to a higher center. Great job keeping her safe!

question: Which of these actions is NOT a way nurses help prevent healthcare-associated infections?

options.A: Prescribing strong antibiotic medications to every new patient
options.B: Changing surgical wound dressings according to hospital policy
options.C: Using sterile technique during invasive urinary catheter insertions
options.D: Practicing consistent hand hygiene before and after patient contact

explanation: Spot on! Nurses don't prescribe drugs, and giving antibiotics to everyone would cause dangerous drug resistance rather than stop infections. Good catch!

question: Your CBI patient has bright red drainage and is crying out with severe lower tummy cramps. What's the most likely issue?

options.A: Rapid healing of the surgical wound inside the bladder
options.B: A blocked catheter trapping fluid and blood clots
options.C: A normal reaction to room-temperature saline solution
options.D: An allergic reaction to the antiseptic skin wipes

explanation: Think of it like a clogged sink: fluid keeps pouring in, but nowhere to go. This stretches the bladder and causes painful cramps.

question: Why must an infant never be left alone in a baby bath tub, even for a split second?

options.A: The water will instantly turn freezing cold without human body heat
options.B: Infants can drown in very shallow water due to lack of head control
options.C: The plastic tub will melt if nobody is touching it
options.D: Infants will climb out of the tub and run down the hospital hallway

explanation: Babies have heavy heads and wobbly necks. They can slip under even an inch of water and inhale fluid in seconds, so never turn your back on them!

question: Why should nurses avoid relying solely on a patient's verbal report about taking their medications?

options.A: Patients often claim they take pills even when they miss them
options.B: Patients never remember the names of their prescribed drugs
options.C: Verbal reports are illegal to record in hospital charts
options.D: Doctors prefer laboratory tests over talking to patients

explanation: Patients want to please their healthcare providers and often say they take their medications faithfully when they actually do not. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h6)

question: In clinical teaching, what does "scaffolding" mean?

options.A: A physical platform used to reach high equipment in simulation labs
options.B: The strict grading rubric used to penalize medication errors
options.C: Temporary support given to a student that is removed as skills improve
options.D: Memorizing drug dosages word-for-word before clinical placement

explanation: Just like builders use temporary scaffolding while putting up a house, your clinical instructors support you closely at first, then gently step back as you gain confidence!

question: Simply put, what is an antigen?

options.A: A protective protein made by B lymphocytes
options.B: A physical barrier found on human skin
options.C: A foreign substance that triggers an immune response
options.D: A type of white blood cell that eats bacteria

explanation: An antigen is basically any foreign tag or molecule on a germ that says 'intruder!' to your immune system, shouting for backup.

question: Why do healthcare workers worry so much about carbapenem-resistant germs?

options.A: Powerful last-resort drugs for severe infections
options.B: Over-the-counter supplements for viral colds
options.C: Mild topical ointments for minor skin rashes
options.D: Preventative vaccines given during childhood

explanation: Carbapenems are our heavy-duty antibiotics. When germs resist them, we are left with very few options in the treatment bag!

question: Why must a nurse check a patient's vital signs before giving certain medications?

options.A: To update the hospital biometric database automatically
options.B: To determine how much the patient's hospital bill will increase
options.C: To fulfill a routine hospital requirement with no clinical value
options.D: To ensure the patient's current status makes the drug safe to give

explanation: Pre-administration assessment catches physiological changes, like low blood pressure or a slow heart rate, that make a scheduled drug unsafe. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T2#GNS125_U4_T2_h3)

question: Why is staff wellness included as a key part of school health programs?

options.A: Teachers serve as role models whose health habits influence students
options.B: Teachers are legally required to pass annual fitness tests
options.C: School staff require more medical leave than regular workers
options.D: Staff members pay for the maintenance of school clinics

explanation: You nailed it! Children copy the adults around them, so healthy teachers naturally encourage good habits in their pupils.

question: When cleaning the female urethral area with antiseptic swabs, which direction should you wipe?

options.A: In a circular scrubbing motion
options.B: From side to side repeatedly
options.C: From back to front
options.D: From front to back

explanation: Always wipe from cleanest to dirtiest—front to back! This keeps nasty bacteria away from the urinary opening.

question: Which of these describes a democratic leadership style in healthcare?

options.A: Making all choices independently without consulting any staff members
options.B: Involving team members in discussions and valuing their input on decisions
options.C: Leaving the ward completely unattended to let nurses work on their own
options.D: Punishing staff members publicly for minor documentation errors

explanation: Democratic leaders bring the team together, listen to everyone's ideas, and make choices collaboratively.

question: What is the main goal of a nurse-patient relationship?

options.A: Promoting the health and recovery of the patient
options.B: Fulfilling social needs of the nursing staff
options.C: Gathering data for hospital financial records
options.D: Building long-lasting personal friendships

explanation: Unlike normal friendships, professional nursing relationships are purposely designed to focus entirely on helping the patient get better. You've got this!

question: Who belongs in an isolation ward rather than a quarantine area?

options.A: Persons who are already sick with confirmed active symptoms
options.B: Community members who missed their routine vaccination
options.C: Family members living in the same house as a sick patient
options.D: Healthy travelers arriving from a country with an ongoing outbreak

explanation: Isolation is specifically reserved for individuals who are currently ill with a contagious disease. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h2)

question: Which circumcision tool uses a small plastic ring tied over the foreskin that eventually falls off on its own?

options.A: Plastibell
options.B: Gomco clamp
options.C: Scalpel blade
options.D: Mogen clamp

explanation: That's the Plastibell! It stays snug on the tissue, cutting off blood supply to the extra skin so it drops off cleanly after a few days as it heals.

question: You walk into the main operating room where a patient's abdomen is open. What must you wear in this restricted zone?

options.A: An isolation gown and sterile gloves only
options.B: Surgical scrubs, head cover, and a surgical mask
options.C: Clean street clothes with a disposable plastic apron
options.D: A lab coat worn over casual clothes

explanation: When heading into the restricted zone, full theatre gear (scrubs, cap, and mask) is a must to keep stray hairs and respiratory droplets away from the sterile field.

question: How does the tetanus toxin cause stiff muscles in a newborn?

options.A: By blocking inhibitory neurotransmitters in the spinal cord
options.B: By destroying the motor nerve endings permanently
options.C: By stopping blood flow to the affected limbs
options.D: By causing massive inflammation in the muscle fibers

explanation: Great job! The toxin blocks calming chemical signals like GABA in the spinal cord, leaving muscles locked in continuous, painful contractions.

question: When is the best time to give pain medicine to a patient about to do physical therapy?

options.A: Only when the patient starts crying from severe pain
options.B: Immediately after the physical therapy session ends
options.C: Right before the patient goes to sleep at night
options.D: About thirty minutes before physical therapy begins

explanation: Giving meds early lets them kick in fully before therapy starts, helping your patient move with much less pain.

question: What is the main goal of Antiretroviral Therapy (ART)?

options.A: To suppress viral replication and reduce the viral load to undetectable levels
options.B: To prevent bacterial infections like pneumonia and tuberculosis
options.C: To completely eliminate the HIV virus from every cell in the body
options.D: To cure advanced stages of AIDS within two weeks of treatment

explanation: While ART doesn't clear every single trace of the virus, it puts a heavy brake on it, lowering the viral load so the immune system can bounce back and stay strong.

question: Which important plasma protein helps hold water inside our blood vessels to prevent swelling?

options.A: Hemoglobin
options.B: Albumin
options.C: Fibrinogen
options.D: Alpha globulin

explanation: You got it! Albumin acts like a sponge inside your blood vessels, pulling on water to keep fluid from leaking out into the body tissues.

question: What is a major plus for local farmers when they use short food supply chains?

options.A: They earn fairer wages by cutting out intermediaries
options.B: They no longer have to harvest their own vegetables
options.C: They rely on international shipping companies to sell crops
options.D: They are forced to sell their products at a massive loss

explanation: Spot on! By removing middlemen and brokers, farmers get to keep a much fairer share of the profit from their sweat and hard work.

question: Globally, where does the highest burden of unsafe medical care usually happen?

options.A: Rural community pharmacies in wealthy nations
options.B: Private specialized clinics in Europe
options.C: Advanced research hospitals in North America
options.D: Low- and middle-income countries

explanation: Resource-limited settings face tough system challenges that unfortunately lead to higher rates of preventable harm.

question: What must happen to qualitative data, like recorded patient interviews, before analysis?

options.A: They must be transcribed word-for-word into written text
options.B: They must be translated into three different foreign languages
options.C: They must be deleted immediately to protect hospital files
options.D: They must be converted entirely into bar charts and graphs

explanation: Audio recordings of interviews need to be written out as text transcripts so researchers can read, code, and analyze the themes. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T3#GNS224_U2_T3_h2)

question: Why is skin protection particularly important during wound and ostomy care in children?

options.A: Adhesive tapes have no effect on young children.
options.B: Infection never occurs around pediatric wounds.
options.C: Pediatric skin is thin, delicate, and prone to breakdown.
options.D: Children produce more sweat than adults do.

explanation: Exactly right! Young skin tears easily and reacts strongly to moisture, friction, and harsh tapes, so handle with extra care. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T11#GNS324_U3_T11_h4)

question: What is the absolute best way to check if a patient is ready to give their own shots at home?

options.A: Ask a family member to take full responsibility for the task
options.B: Provide a written multiple-choice test on injection theory
options.C: Have the patient perform a return demonstration of the steps
options.D: Ask the patient to read the medication package insert aloud

explanation: Seeing is believing! Having them show you how they do it lets you coach them, build their confidence, and make sure they are doing it safely.

question: How does a new mother's body mainly get rid of extra pregnancy fluids right after birth?

options.A: Through increased production of bile acids
options.B: Through reabsorption into the bone marrow
options.C: Through heavy urination and sweating
options.D: Through rapid shedding of stomach lining

explanation: Peeing and sweating a lot in the first few days postpartum is totally normal—it's just the body's way of flushing out the extra pregnancy fluids!

question: A nurse reviews a high-quality study on a new pain management protocol. What local factor must be checked before introducing it to the ward?

options.A: Whether the ward has the staff training and resources to support the protocol
options.B: How many awards the primary investigator has won
options.C: Whether the original authors will visit the hospital to supervise
options.D: If the journal article has a colorful cover page

explanation: Research implementation must always consider local feasibility, including equipment, staff readiness, and institutional support. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T4#GNS224_U4_T4_h6)

question: In the theatre team, who is mainly responsible for writing down the counts on the whiteboard?

options.A: The lead surgeon
options.B: The scrub nurse
options.C: The anesthetist
options.D: The circulating nurse

explanation: The circulating nurse is outside the sterile field (unsterile zone), which makes them the perfect person to maintain the official tally board.

question: Why is the hypophysial portal system so important for hormone control?

options.A: It allows brain hormones to reach the pituitary gland without being diluted in the main bloodstream
options.B: It cools down the hypothalamus when body temperature rises during a fever
options.C: It stores excess neurohormones until the body requires emergency fight-or-flight responses
options.D: It prevents hormones from the pituitary gland from entering the general circulation

explanation: This direct pathway acts like a private express lane, making sure brain hormones get straight to the pituitary gland in strong, concentrated doses without getting lost in the wider body circulation.

question: Which sign strongly suggests a patient is struggling to swallow during a meal?

options.A: Asking for a glass of clean water
options.B: Finishing the meal within ten minutes
options.C: A gurgling voice right after swallowing
options.D: Chewing food slowly on one side

explanation: Spot on! A wet or gurgling voice means food or drink slipped into the upper airway. Good eye spotting that!

question: Which of these is NOT a major challenge facing formal home health care in Nigeria?

options.A: Inadequate road infrastructure slowing down nurse transit
options.B: Universal government funding covering all home care services
options.C: Shortage of a unified national health policy for home care
options.D: Public preference for traditional healing methods in some areas

explanation: Universal government funding for home care doesn't exist here yet! Most people pay out-of-pocket, making funding a major hurdle, not a reality.

question: How do acquired bleeding problems differ from inherited conditions like hemophilia?

options.A: Acquired disorders develop later in life due to illnesses or deficiencies
options.B: Inherited disorders only show up during major surgery in adulthood
options.C: Inherited disorders can be cured easily with simple vitamin supplements
options.D: Acquired disorders only affect red blood cells instead of platelets

explanation: While inherited conditions are passed down in your genes from birth, acquired disorders pop up later in life because of illness, poor nutrition, or certain medications.

question: What are the two main components that make up the cardiovascular system?

options.A: The brain and spinal cord
options.B: The heart and blood vessels
options.C: The lungs and airways
options.D: The kidneys and bladder

explanation: The cardiovascular system is composed of the heart, which acts as the pump, and blood vessels, which serve as the delivery pipes. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h1)

question: What does intersectoral collaboration mean in community health practice?

options.A: Transferring all sick patients directly to tertiary teaching hospitals without delay
options.B: Working together with non-health sectors like agriculture and education to improve health
options.C: Merging all community health clinics under one central government ministry
options.D: Requiring nurses to perform the duties of doctors and pharmacists simultaneously

explanation: Intersectoral collaboration involves partnering with different sectors outside health because social determinants of health span multiple fields. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T26#GNS225_U2_T26_h7)

question: What is the main difference between recording and reporting in the clinic?

options.A: Recording is writing down individual patient care, while reporting is summarizing data for higher health authorities.
options.B: Recording is done by doctors only while reporting is for nurses.
options.C: Recording uses electronic tablets while reporting uses paper only.
options.D: Recording happens once a year and reporting happens daily.

explanation: Think of recording as capturing what you do with one patient in front of you, while reporting is putting all those numbers together to send upstream so the government can plan public health! You've got this.

question: What is the primary purpose of government food assistance programs?

options.A: To force citizens to purchase locally grown organic vegetables
options.B: To regulate the exact calorie intake of every household
options.C: To completely eliminate the need for private grocery stores
options.D: To help protect vulnerable populations from hunger and poor nutrition

explanation: Social safety nets exist to ensure that low-income families and individuals can access enough food to stay healthy. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T020#GNS227_U2_T020_h7)

question: In the epidemiological triangle, stagnant water sitting outside during the rainy season represents which component?

options.A: Agent
options.B: Host
options.C: Environment
options.D: Reservoir

explanation: That's right! External surroundings, weather conditions, and water sources are all part of the environmental piece of the puzzle.

question: What causes the movement called restitution right after the baby's head is born?

options.A: The shoulders push past the perineum simultaneously
options.B: The mother pushes extra hard to clear the airway
options.C: The midwife manually turns the baby to check for breathing
options.D: The head untwists to realign with the shoulders inside the pelvis

explanation: Brilliant! Restitution is just the head naturally untwisting and straightening out with the shoulders after it pops out.

question: What is the main reason for involving community and religious leaders in youth health programs?

options.A: To diagnose complex tropical diseases in children
options.B: To prescribe medication during nursing staff shortages
options.C: To build cultural acceptance and reduce community resistance
options.D: To manage the financial accounts of the clinic

explanation: Community leaders hold great influence. Bringing them on board helps secure local backing and prevents cultural pushback against sensitive topics.

question: Which agency is responsible for regulating food and dietary supplements in Nigeria?

options.A: FMOH
options.B: Standard Organisation of Nigeria
options.C: WHO
options.D: NAFDAC

explanation: NAFDAC is our local body that keeps us safe by regulating drugs, food, and supplements in Nigeria. Great to keep in mind for clinical practice!

question: Why do nurses ask patients about how many pads or tampons they use when assessing heavy periods?

options.A: It reveals the exact day ovulation occurred during the previous month.
options.B: It determines whether the patient has reached early menopause.
options.C: It measures the exact size and muscular strength of the uterus.
options.D: It helps estimate the actual amount of blood lost.

explanation: Since everyone's definition of 'heavy' is different, counting pads gives you a practical, objective way to measure blood loss.

question: Why does a hospital ward have separate clean utility and dirty utility rooms?

options.A: To comply with fire safety evacuation rules
options.B: To give nurses a private space to take meal breaks
options.C: To separate male patients from female patients
options.D: To prevent cross-contamination between sterile supplies and waste

explanation: Separation ensures clean medical supplies do not mix with used equipment, body fluids, or waste items. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h2)

question: What is the main goal of providing antenatal care right inside a mother's home?

options.A: To bring essential pregnancy monitoring and support to the mother's doorstep
options.B: To replace all hospital deliveries permanently
options.C: To reduce the workload of urban doctors
options.D: To eliminate the need for any laboratory tests during pregnancy

explanation: Home visits (domiciliary care) are all about making sure pregnant women get basic antenatal checks right where they live. You've got this!

question: What is the main goal of safe motherhood initiatives?

options.A: To minimize the total cost of obstetric medications
options.B: To ensure all births occur strictly inside tertiary hospitals
options.C: To reduce preventable maternal and newborn deaths
options.D: To completely eliminate pregnancy for high-risk women

explanation: You've got this! Safe motherhood is all about keeping both mum and baby safe and healthy by stopping complications before they get out of hand.

question: Which part of the foetal body receives the highest concentration of freshly oxygenated blood?

options.A: The brain and heart
options.B: The gastrointestinal tract
options.C: The lower extremities
options.D: The lungs and trachea

explanation: The foramen ovale directs the freshest, most oxygen-rich blood toward the upper body to support the rapidly growing brain and heart. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T8#GNS121_U6_T8_h4)

question: What is the primary function of lymph nodes?

options.A: Filtering lymph and trapping foreign invaders
options.B: Producing new red blood cells
options.C: Pumping lymph fluid through the body
options.D: Storing excess dietary fats

explanation: Lymph nodes act as filters that catch bacteria, viruses, and debris before fluid returns to the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h3)

question: What is a key focus of antenatal care specifically for pregnant teenagers?

options.A: Nutritional support and close monitoring for anemia and hypertension
options.B: Encouraging unassisted home deliveries to lower hospital costs
options.C: Avoiding all physical exercise throughout the entire pregnancy
options.D: Strict community isolation to avoid social stigma and gossip

explanation: Correct! Since teens are still growing themselves, they need extra nutrition and close checks for blood pressure and iron levels. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T12#GNS312_U3_T12_h5)

question: Which practice should nurses avoid when handling used injection needles?

options.A: Activating the safety device
options.B: Dropping it straight into a bin
options.C: Carrying it in a dedicated tray
options.D: Recapping the needle by hand

explanation: Recapping needles by hand is a major cause of accidental needlestick injuries and should never be done. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h8)

question: What is the primary danger associated with polypharmacy in older patients?

options.A: Complete elimination of side effects from strong painkillers
options.B: A high likelihood of adverse drug reactions and harmful interactions
options.C: Rapid improvement in cognitive processing speed and memory
options.D: Immediate cure of all existing chronic and acute health conditions

explanation: Taking many different medicines at once greatly increases the chance that they will interact badly with each other or cause harmful side effects. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T8#GNS225_U5_T8_h6)

question: Why do we keep a patient with swallowing trouble sitting upright for 30 minutes after a meal?

options.A: To help the digestive system burn extra calories faster
options.B: To allow the jaw muscles time to rest after chewing
options.C: To prevent the backflow of food and reduce the risk of aspiration into the lungs
options.D: To improve the absorption of vitamins in the small intestine

explanation: Gravity is our best friend here! Keeping them upright gives the stomach time to settle so food doesn't creep back up toward the airway.

question: During a serum sickness reaction, where do the troublesome immune complexes usually get trapped?

options.A: Directly on brain cell surfaces
options.B: In small blood vessels and tissues
options.C: Inside large heart valves
options.D: Within the hard bone matrix

explanation: These complexes love to settle down in the tiny filtering blood vessels of places like your joints and skin, causing irritation.

question: Where is the scheduled date for a child's next vaccine dose primarily recorded for the mother to see?

options.A: On the pharmacy prescription ledger
options.B: On the child's home-based health card
options.C: In the national budget allocation report
options.D: In the local government tax receipt

explanation: The child health card stays with the caregiver and serves as the primary personal reminder for upcoming immunization dates. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T74#GNS214_U1_T74_h3)

question: Why is oxytocin given right after a baby is delivered?

options.A: To stimulate early breastmilk letdown
options.B: To lower the mother's blood pressure
options.C: To speed up the dilation of the cervix
options.D: To prevent postpartum hemorrhage

explanation: Spot on! Oxytocin makes the uterus clamp down firmly, sealing off blood vessels and keeping heavy bleeding at bay.

question: A patient says they want to save their leftover antibiotics for next time. What should you tell them?

options.A: Suggest sharing the remaining pills with family members who catch colds
options.B: Confirm that keeping extra drugs handy saves money on clinic visits
options.C: Explain that incomplete or saved doses promote drug resistance and treatment failure
options.D: Advise the patient to store the leftover capsules in a dark refrigerator

explanation: Always gently correct this common myth! Saving or sharing leftover drugs leads to under-dosing, which is a fast track to creating resistant superbugs. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T92#GNS214_U1_T92_h6)

question: Why do joint contractures happen in patients with severe paralysis?

options.A: Nerves regenerate too quickly and pull the joints out of place
options.B: Joint cartilage dissolves from lack of blood circulation
options.C: Bones grow too fast because they do not bear any body weight
options.D: Muscles and tendons shorten due to a lack of movement and stretching

explanation: If a joint isn't moved through its range of motion, the soft tissues adapt by shrinking up, freezing the joint in one position.

question: Why is the agricultural sector so important when health workers try to improve nutrition?

options.A: Because farming practices have no impact on community health outcomes
options.B: Because farmers are legally required to diagnose nutritional deficiencies
options.C: Because agricultural workers manage all rural health clinics
options.D: Because agriculture determines how much and what types of food are produced

explanation: Brilliant! Farming dictates what food is available and how varied the food supply is, making agriculture the very foundation of good nutrition.

question: What do we call the process of forming mature sperm cells in the male testes?

options.A: Fertilization
options.B: Spermatogenesis
options.C: Gastrulation
options.D: Oogenesis

explanation: Spermatogenesis is just the medical term for how sperm cells are made in the testes. Think: 'spermato-' for sperm and '-genesis' for creation!

question: Which phase of cancer development involves a permanent change or mutation in a cell's DNA?

options.A: Initiation
options.B: Progression
options.C: Metastasis
options.D: Promotion

explanation: You nailed it! Initiation is always step one—it's the very first moment a trigger causes a permanent genetic change in a normal cell.

question: Why does your digestion temporarily slow down when you are suddenly startled or stressed?

options.A: The stomach stops working permanently due to shock
options.B: Food intake automatically increases during stressful times
options.C: Energy is diverted to muscles and vital organs for defense
options.D: Digestive enzymes turn into stress hormones instantly

explanation: Your body is smart! When danger hits, it pulls energy away from digesting food and sends it straight to your muscles so you can react fast.

question: What tool do public health officials mainly use to track FGM rates across Nigeria?

options.A: Federal Customs Import Records
options.B: Primary School Attendance Sheets
options.C: Demographic and Health Surveys
options.D: National Electoral Voting Registers

explanation: Correct! Health surveys give us reliable statistical data on how common FGM is and how trends are shifting across different regions.

question: Why do doctors order genetic tests like FISH or karyotyping for blood cancers?

options.A: To find the patient's blood group for a transfusion
options.B: To find specific chromosome changes and gene mutations
options.C: To measure how much blood was lost in surgery
options.D: To see how fast red blood cells settle in a tube

explanation: Looking at the genetic makeup of the cancer cells helps the medical team figure out the best treatment plan for the patient.

question: What does a low p-value (less than 0.05) usually let a researcher do?

options.A: Reject the null hypothesis
options.B: Change the independent variable
options.C: Eliminate all confounding factors
options.D: Ignore ethical review boards

explanation: A low p-value means your findings are statistically significant and unlikely to just be a stroke of luck!

question: What dangerous drug interaction must you warn patients about when taking ED meds like sildenafil (Viagra)?

options.A: Taking them with dairy products causes permanent blindness
options.B: Combining them with organic nitrates causes severe hypotension
options.C: Swallowing them with fruit juice stops their absorption entirely
options.D: Mixing them with aspirin causes sudden kidney failure

question: How do you acquire knowledge through the empirical method?

options.A: Through direct observation and sensory experience
options.B: Through pure logical thought without looking at the patient
options.C: By accepting traditional beliefs without testing
options.D: By waiting for a sudden gut feeling or intuition

explanation: Empiricism means gathering facts using your own senses—like looking at a wound, touching a pulse, or listening to lung sounds.

question: What is the main job of the tough outer shell (exoskeleton) on an insect?

options.A: Generating body heat during cold weather
options.B: Pumping oxygen directly into the insect bloodstream
options.C: Protecting internal organs and preventing water loss
options.D: Producing venom to paralyze small prey

explanation: That crunchy outer coat acts like a suit of armor that keeps the insect safe and stops it from drying out in the sun.

question: A patient has surgery to remove a bowel tumor just to relieve an active intestinal blockage. What type of surgery is this?

options.A: Diagnostic
options.B: Curative
options.C: Prophylactic
options.D: Palliative

explanation: Well done! Even though it's surgery, it's classified as palliative because its main job is to ease distressing symptoms (like a blockage) rather than cure the cancer itself.

question: Why do we check the Rhesus blood group for a patient having an incomplete abortion?

options.A: To calculate her exact gestational age
options.B: To check for severe iron deficiency anemia
options.C: To find out if she has a bacterial infection
options.D: To see if she needs anti-D immunoglobulin

explanation: If a mother is Rhesus-negative, giving anti-D immunoglobulin protects her future pregnancies from blood-type mismatch issues. Great clinical thinking!

question: Which simple nursing care measure helps soothe irritated vulval tissue and keep the area clean?

options.A: Using scented talcum powder daily
options.B: Scrubbing the area with harsh antiseptic soap
options.C: Applying dry heat packs directly to the skin
options.D: Sitz baths with plain warm water

explanation: Warm sitz baths are a nurse's best friend here—they gently clean the area and soothe discomfort without using harsh chemicals that make irritation worse. Beautiful nursing care!

question: Why do patients with diabetes need frequent blood sugar checks after an abortion?

options.A: Insulin is no longer effective after surgery
options.B: Physical stress and hormonal shifts cause rapid sugar changes
options.C: Abortion procedures automatically cure diabetes
options.D: Blood sugar levels always drop to zero

explanation: Physical stress and changing hormones make blood sugar levels bounce around, making them much harder to control during recovery.

question: What is the primary goal of medical detoxification in substance abuse care?

options.A: To isolate the patient from all family members during therapy
options.B: To teach the patient new vocational skills for finding employment
options.C: To permanently cure the psychological desire to use drugs again
options.D: To safely clear the substance from the body while managing withdrawal symptoms

explanation: Spot on! Detox is all about physical stabilization—getting the drug out of the system safely while doctors and nurses help manage the rough withdrawal symptoms.

question: How are minerals fundamentally different from vitamins?

options.A: Minerals are only found in pills, while vitamins come from plants
options.B: Minerals are inorganic elements, whereas vitamins are organic compounds
options.C: Minerals provide energy calories, whereas vitamins do not
options.D: Minerals dissolve in fat, whereas vitamins dissolve in water

explanation: Minerals like iron and calcium come straight from the earth and water (inorganic), whereas vitamins are made by living things (organic). Easy to remember once you link minerals to rocks and soil!

question: How do contact tracing and patient interviews help during an outbreak?

options.A: They instantly give immunity to everyone who gets interviewed
options.B: They replace the need to run lab tests on blood samples
options.C: They stop germs from changing into stronger strains
options.D: They help track down the original source and anyone else who might be exposed

explanation: By talking to patients and tracing their steps, we can find out where they got sick and who else needs to be checked.

question: Why is it dangerous to just silence an infusion pump alarm and walk away?

options.A: Unresolved alarms cause the pump to reverse fluid flow into the bag
options.B: It can delay necessary treatment or fail to catch a dangerous blockage
options.C: Hospital policy fines staff members who touch alarms too quickly
options.D: The pump will automatically erase all patient data if silenced

explanation: You got it! Alarms are there for a reason. Ignoring them without fixing the root cause can leave your patient without their meds or miss a serious line problem.

question: How does a Root Cause Analysis differ from simply blaming an individual worker?

options.A: It focuses exclusively on financial losses rather than clinical outcomes
options.B: It investigates underlying systemic flaws rather than stopping at personal fault
options.C: It ensures that the guilty employee is fired immediately without appeal
options.D: It hides safety mistakes from hospital management and regulatory bodies

explanation: Root Cause Analysis asks 'Why did this happen?' instead of 'Who did this?'. It digs deep into workflow, equipment, and communication to fix the real problem.

question: Which tool do nurses commonly use to screen for depression in older adults?

options.A: Body Mass Index calculator
options.B: Glasgow Coma Scale
options.C: Apgar scoring system
options.D: Geriatric Depression Scale

explanation: The Geriatric Depression Scale is tailored specifically to catch depressive symptoms in seniors. You're building solid clinical skills!

question: What marks the transition period of adolescence?

options.A: Fixed behavioral patterns
options.B: The cessation of brain development
options.C: Complete emotional and financial independence
options.D: Rapid physical, emotional, and social changes

explanation: Adolescence is defined as a transitional phase marked by rapid changes across physical, emotional, and social domains. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T13#GNS312_U3_T13_h1)

question: An HIV-positive mum asks if she can give her two-month-old baby sips of plain water during hot weather. What is your best response as a nurse?

options.A: Suggest replacing one daily breastfeed with clean water to test tolerance
options.B: Encourage small amounts of boiled water to prevent dehydration in the heat
options.C: Advise against water because it can damage the gut lining and increase HIV transmission risk
options.D: Approve the water provided it is boiled and cooled beforehand

explanation: Even simple water can disrupt a baby's delicate tummy lining, making it easier for the virus to pass through. Stick to exclusive breastfeeding!

question: Why must nurses always teach postpartum women to clean their perineal area from front to back?

options.A: To stimulate faster contraction of the abdominal wall muscles
options.B: To ensure that lochia stops flowing within the first twenty-four hours
options.C: To prevent spreading bacteria from the anal region into the vagina or wound
options.D: To prevent painful swelling of the lower extremities

explanation: Wiping front to back keeps unwanted germs from the back passage away from healing tears or surgical stitches, preventing nasty infections! Simple hygiene makes a massive difference. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h7)

question: What is the main focus of occupational therapy in subacute care?

options.A: Helping patients perform daily self-care tasks like dressing and bathing
options.B: Managing complex intravenous medications and wound dressings
options.C: Assessing nutritional intake and feeding tube placement needs
options.D: Restoring walking ability and lower body muscle strength

explanation: You nailed it! Occupational therapy focuses on helping clients get back to doing everyday activities independently.

question: What is a major challenge in providing adolescent reproductive care in many communities?

options.A: The requirement that all nurses undergo legal training before practice
options.B: A complete lack of teenage patients visiting urban health facilities
options.C: Conflict between traditional moral disapproval and young people's health needs
options.D: An absolute nationwide ban on importing any modern contraceptive items

explanation: Cultural and religious beliefs often clash with the clinical reality that teens need reproductive health support. Navigating this is part of nursing!

question: In ventilator settings, what does the acronym PEEP stand for?

options.A: Peak External Exhalational Parameter
options.B: Pulmonary End-Ejection Pressure
options.C: Positive End-Expiratory Pressure
options.D: Primary Expiratory Expansion Protocol

explanation: PEEP keeps a tiny bit of pressure in the tiny air sacs (alveoli) at the very end of a breath so they don't collapse on themselves. You're doing great!

question: What goes wrong in hyperproliferative skin conditions like psoriasis?

options.A: Skin cells multiply much faster than normal and pile up on the surface
options.B: Melanocytes completely disappear from the deepest layer of the dermis
options.C: Sebaceous glands shut down, leaving the skin completely dry and scaly
options.D: Skin cells stop growing entirely, causing deep chronic ulcerations

explanation: Well done! In conditions like psoriasis, cells grow way too fast, creating those thick, raised patches on the skin.

question: An older adult has weak muscles and is getting ready to leave the hospital. What is the most important step to prevent falls?

options.A: Removing all windows from the patient's home environment
options.B: Ensuring the patient has proper instruction in using an assistive device
options.C: Restricting the patient to bed rest to prevent any movement
options.D: Encouraging the patient to walk barefoot indoors for better grip

explanation: Walking aids like canes or walkers only work if the patient knows how to use them safely and confidently!

question: What is the main goal of giving ovulation-stimulating medications like clomiphene citrate?

options.A: To thicken the uterine lining permanently
options.B: To clear blocked fallopian tubes
options.C: To increase male testosterone levels
options.D: To encourage the release of mature eggs

explanation: These helpful drugs nudge the ovaries to develop and release eggs when a woman's ovulation is irregular.

question: A patient has trouble swallowing (dysphagia) after a stroke. What kind of fluids are they likely given?

options.A: Thickened liquids to prevent choking and aspiration
options.B: Completely clear water to test immediate swallowing speed
options.C: Unrestricted fluids served through a wide straw
options.D: Hot liquids to stimulate throat nerve endings

explanation: Thin water runs down too fast for weak throat muscles. Thickened liquids travel slower, giving the patient time to swallow safely without choking.

question: What is a major goal of physical therapy in the long-term management of a child with spastic cerebral palsy?

options.A: Eliminating the need for any assistive devices by age five
options.B: Preventing joint contractures and improving functional mobility
options.C: Permanently stopping all involuntary muscle contractions
options.D: Curing the underlying brain lesion through intense exercise

explanation: Physical therapy uses stretching, strengthening, and positioning to keep muscles pliable and prevent permanent joint tightening. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T4#GNS324_U4_T4_h6)

question: A nurse manager holds a team meeting just to check on staff morale and listen to personal concerns. Which theory supports this?

options.A: Classical Command Theory
options.B: Scientific Management
options.C: Human Relations Theory
options.D: Bureaucratic Theory

explanation: The human relations approach reminds us that workers have social and emotional needs, and keeping morale high makes a huge difference.

question: Why do midwives check both cervical dilation and moulding together on the partograph?

options.A: Cervical dilation causes the skull bones to separate rather than overlap
options.B: A baby may have a normal cervix opening while the head remains stuck due to poor fit
options.C: Good moulding always guarantees that the baby will be delivered within one hour
options.D: Moulding only occurs during the third stage of active labour after the cervix is fully open
