question: Why do nursing schools connect classroom lectures with clinical ward postings?

options.A: To help you apply what you read in textbooks to real patients
options.B: To cut down the number of hours you spend in school
options.C: To replace tests with chats by the patient's bedside
options.D: To keep students away from the school campus

explanation: Bridging theory and practice helps you understand the real 'why' behind the bedside care you give to your patients.

question: How long should a nurse stay right by the patient's side after a blood transfusion starts?

options.A: Only until the pump is turned on
options.B: The first 15 minutes
options.C: Until the entire bag is empty
options.D: The first two hours

explanation: Most serious transfusion reactions happen fast at the very beginning. Staying close for those first 15 minutes lets you catch and treat any reaction early!

question: What is the primary characteristic of individuals who are placed in quarantine?

options.A: They are healthcare workers returning from a high-risk assignment.
options.B: They are currently healthy but have been exposed to a contagious disease.
options.C: They have laboratory-confirmed illness and active symptoms.
options.D: They refuse to take mandatory routine immunizations.

explanation: Quarantine is strictly meant for exposed individuals who do not yet show active signs of illness. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h1)

question: A nurse wears gloves while emptying a patient's urinary catheter bag. Which link in the chain of infection is the nurse primarily trying to break?

options.A: Reservoir
options.B: Infectious agent
options.C: Mode of transmission
options.D: Susceptible host

explanation: Wearing gloves creates a barrier that stops germs from moving from the urine to the nurse's hands and onto other surfaces or patients. [learn more](GST114_U1_T3#GST114_U1_T3_h2)

question: What is the main job of a receptor in a reflex pathway?

options.A: Contraction of skeletal muscle fibers
options.B: Releasing hormones directly into the bloodstream
options.C: Converting physical stimuli into electrical nerve signals
options.D: Processing complex thoughts in the cerebral cortex

explanation: Receptors act like translators, changing physical stuff like heat or touch into the electrical language that nerves can understand.

question: How has our view of leadership in healthcare changed over time?

options.A: From team collaboration to absolute individual control by doctors
options.B: From flexible behaviors to rigid, unchanging personal traits
options.C: From clinical skills to purely financial management tasks
options.D: From fixed personal traits to flexible behaviors and situational responses

explanation: We used to think leaders were just born with special traits. Now, we know good leaders adapt their style to fit whatever is happening on the ward!

question: What is the main difference between short-acting and long-acting corticosteroids?

options.A: How long they remain active in the body and their strength.
options.B: Whether they require a doctor's prescription.
options.C: If they cause weight gain during long-term therapy.
options.D: Whether they are swallowed or injected into a muscle.

explanation: You got it! Different steroid types stay in the system for different lengths of time and have varying strengths for reducing swelling.

question: When is it okay to leave a smart bed's wheel brakes unlocked?

options.A: When the patient is sleeping soundly through the night
options.B: Whenever the bed exit alarm system is fully armed
options.C: Only when the bed is actively being transported
options.D: During routine morning bed baths and linen changes

explanation: Always keep brakes locked! The only exception is when you are actively wheeling the bed down the hallway to a new room.

question: A patient is given naloxone to wake them up and reverse a dangerous morphine overdose. What kind of drug action is this?

options.A: Absorption
options.B: Potentiation
options.C: Antagonism
options.D: Synergism

explanation: Spot on! Naloxone acts as a true antagonist—it rushes to the rescue, kicks the morphine off the receptors, and blocks its effects to save the patient.

question: Why should you separate normal general waste from hazardous medical waste right from the start?

options.A: It ensures all waste can be recycled together safely.
options.B: It eliminates the need for any protective gear during disposal.
options.C: It reduces the volume of expensive hazardous waste treatment.
options.D: It allows general waste to be incinerated at high temperatures.

explanation: Treating medical waste safely is very costly. Keeping ordinary rubbish separate stops us from spending extra money and wasting precious resources on treating harmless items!

question: What is the primary focus of medical care for a patient diagnosed with CJD?

options.A: Relieving symptoms and providing comfort
options.B: Stopping the replication of prions
options.C: Restoring lost memory and brain cells
options.D: Reversing the genetic mutation

explanation: Correct! Because there is currently no cure for CJD, treatment is all about palliative care—keeping the patient comfortable and easing their symptoms.

question: Which of these checks is a key part of a neurovascular assessment on an injured arm or leg?

options.A: Total daily fluid intake and urine output
options.B: Bowel sound frequency and abdominal tone
options.C: Peripheral pulses and capillary refill
options.D: Client baseline blood cholesterol levels

explanation: Well done! Neurovascular checks are all about blood flow, feeling, and movement. Checking pulses and capillary refill tells us if blood is reaching the fingers and toes.

question: What is the easiest and most sensitive way for a nurse to check for early fluid buildup at home?

options.A: Weighing the patient daily at the same time
options.B: Measuring the circumference of the arm
options.C: Asking the patient if they feel thirsty
options.D: Checking shoe size once a week

explanation: Water weighs a lot! A sudden climb on the bathroom scale is almost always the earliest sign that fluid is starting to build up in the body.

question: When prioritizing health issues in a community, what does 'magnitude' mean?

options.A: The distance from the village to the nearest hospital
options.B: The number of people affected by the health problem
options.C: The total financial cost of medical treatment
options.D: The physical size of the local health clinic

explanation: Exactly right! Magnitude simply tells you how widespread the issue is—how many community members are actually dealing with it.

question: Why does early teenage pregnancy often negatively impact a young person's future?

options.A: It directly impairs cognitive functioning and memory
options.B: It automatically causes permanent physical disability in all young mothers
options.C: It frequently interrupts their education and limits economic opportunities
options.D: It permanently removes all support from their extended families

explanation: Parenthood during adolescence often forces teenagers to drop out of school, making it much harder to gain the skills needed for stable employment later in life. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T9#GNS312_U3_T9_h1)

question: Where does fluid from the very tip of the tongue first drain into the lymphatic system?

options.A: Submandibular lymph nodes
options.B: Jugulodigastric lymph nodes
options.C: Submental lymph nodes
options.D: Superficial parotid nodes

explanation: The submental nodes sit right under your chin, making them the first stop for lymphatic drainage from the very tip of the tongue.

question: Which substance must be present in a rehydration solution to help activate the SGLT1 transporter in the gut?

options.A: Glucose
options.B: Potassium
options.C: Bicarbonate
options.D: Protein

explanation: Think of glucose as a helpful partner! It teams up with sodium to attach to the SGLT1 transporter, which helps pull both molecules into the intestinal cells.

question: A woman who took oral medications for Type 2 diabetes for five years becomes pregnant. How is her condition classified?

options.A: Transient pregnancy hyperglycemia
options.B: Pregestational diabetes mellitus
options.C: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.D: Secondary placental diabetes

explanation: Because she had diagnosed diabetes and took medications before getting pregnant, her condition is classified as pregestational diabetes. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T006#GNS226_U4_T006_h2)

question: What does the clinician usually do right before cutting the skin with the scalpel?

options.A: Elevating a small cone of skin using a sterile needle
options.B: Applying deep pressure to stop all local circulation
options.C: Stretching the skin tightly in four opposite directions
options.D: Massaging the area vigorously to numb it faster

explanation: Correct! Lifting a tiny tent of skin helps the clinician snip just the right top layer safely without cutting too deep.

question: A patient with an arm cast complains of an intense itch deep inside. What advice should you give?

options.A: Pour a small amount of baby oil down the cast opening to soothe the skin
options.B: Insert a clean knitting needle gently down the side to scratch the itchy spot
options.C: Use a cool hair dryer breeze directed into the cast opening to relieve itching
options.D: Submerge the entire arm in warm soapy water until the itching stops

explanation: A cool breeze from a hair dryer is a safe trick to ease itching. Never stick objects inside the cast—they can break skin or get stuck!

question: What is the main goal of medical treatment for someone with hyperthyroidism?

options.A: Replacing deficient thyroid hormones with synthetic T4
options.B: Blocking all adrenaline receptors in the central nervous system
options.C: Permanently destroying the thyroid gland using chemical agents
options.D: Restoring a normal metabolic state known as euthyroidism

explanation: We want to bring those high hormone levels back down to a healthy, balanced state called euthyroidism. You've got this!

question: A mother is scared that immunization injections will make her baby sick. How should you respond?

options.A: Scold her for ignoring professional medical advice
options.B: Explain normal mild side effects and reassure her about the benefits
options.C: Advise her to skip the injections entirely if she feels worried
options.D: Tell her that children never experience any discomfort from vaccines

explanation: Moms often worry! Taking a moment to calmly explain normal side effects like low fever builds great trust and helps keep babies on schedule.

question: Why is 'modifiability' an important factor when deciding which health problem to tackle first?

options.A: It proves that chronic diseases are always easier to cure than acute infections
options.B: It eliminates the need for community participation in health planning
options.C: It guarantees that the local government will increase taxes for health programs
options.D: It ensures the team focuses on problems that can realistically be solved with available resources

explanation: Modifiability looks at whether an intervention can actually make a difference given current technology, funding, and staff capacity. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h8)

question: Why is involving men in family health beneficial for the household?

options.A: It improves health outcomes for women and children
options.B: It reduces the household income requirement
options.C: It makes clinic visits shorter for everyone
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for nurses

explanation: Active male participation creates a supportive environment that directly boosts health and wellness for mothers and children. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h1)

question: Which of these is an example of a capital budget expense in a hospital?

options.A: Buying disposable syringes for the emergency ward
options.B: Purchasing a brand-new CT scanner
options.C: Paying the monthly electricity bill for the pharmacy
options.D: Covering the weekly wages of ward support staff

explanation: Think of capital budgets as the big fund for expensive, long-lasting equipment and heavy machinery like a CT scanner, rather than daily supplies.

question: A 30-year smoker comes in with severe breathlessness and a chronic cough. Which condition affecting the tiny air sacs is most likely the cause?

options.A: Acute bronchitis
options.B: Bacterial pneumonia
options.C: Emphysema
options.D: Pulmonary embolism

explanation: Long-term smoking destroys the delicate walls of the alveoli (air sacs), leading to emphysema and trapped air. You're building solid clinical instincts!

question: Why is it so important for a nurse to ask a patient to demonstrate how they use their inhaler?

options.A: To check if the patient is strong enough to crush the capsule
options.B: To measure how fast the patient can blow air into a balloon
options.C: To ensure the patient bought the correct brand of medication
options.D: To catch hidden errors that could prevent the medicine from working

explanation: It's easy for patients to pick up little habits over time that stop the medicine from working right. Seeing them do it live is the best way to help them correct it!

question: Why is high blood pressure often called a 'silent killer'?

options.A: It stops the heart completely without warning signs.
options.B: It causes sudden deafness before any physical pain starts.
options.C: It rarely produces early symptoms until serious organ damage occurs.
options.D: It only strikes individuals while they are fast asleep at night.

explanation: You got it! High blood pressure can quietly damage the body for years without any warning signs, which is why regular checks are so important.

question: What is the main difference between a regular hospital bed and a smart bed?

options.A: Smart beds require manual hand cranks for all adjustments
options.B: Smart beds are exclusively used in outpatient surgical clinics
options.C: Smart beds integrate computerized systems and sensors for monitoring
options.D: Smart beds cannot be adjusted for patient height or seating angles

explanation: Smart beds are great because they have built-in sensors and computer tech to track patient vitals automatically, unlike old-school manual beds!

question: Why do many patients with severe, long-term lung disease experience noticeable weight loss and muscle wasting?

options.A: The physical effort of breathing uses up enormous amounts of energy
options.B: Their digestive tracts stop absorbing nutrients completely
options.C: They deliberately avoid eating to prevent shortness of breath
options.D: Liver damage prevents them from storing body fat

explanation: Think about how hard it is to run a race—now imagine working that hard just to breathe all day! That heavy effort burns massive amounts of energy and leads to weight loss.

question: How should a freshly applied Plaster of Paris cast be supported while it dries?

options.A: Covered tightly with heavy warm blankets to trap heat
options.B: Suspended vertically by a rope attached to the ceiling
options.C: Lying directly flat on a hard wooden examination table
options.D: Resting on soft pillows with open air circulation

explanation: Soft pillows cradle the wet cast and support its shape without pressing flat, damaging spots into the drying plaster.

question: Why can it be dangerous to combine an expectorant with a cough suppressant?

options.A: It can trap thinned mucus in the airways if the patient cannot cough
options.B: It leads to severe kidney failure within twenty-four hours
options.C: It completely neutralizes the chemical structure of both drugs
options.D: It causes an immediate and dangerous drop in the patient's heart rate

explanation: Think about it: if the drug turns the mucus watery but you stop the patient from coughing, that fluid gets trapped and blocks their airway. Dangerous combo!

question: What type of liability do nurse managers usually face if they do a poor job with staffing or hiring?

options.A: Strict criminal liability for patient readmissions
options.B: Direct liability for administrative negligence
options.C: Absolute immunity from all civil court proceedings
options.D: Vicarious liability for every bedside drug error

explanation: Managers have specific administrative duties like vetting staff properly. If they fail here, they face direct liability for their own poor management.

question: Which sign tells you a limb with a tight, wrapping (circumferential) burn is developing compartment syndrome?

options.A: Sudden appearance of localized skin blisters
options.B: Hyperactive bowel sounds and abdominal pain
options.C: Elevated core body temperature and chills
options.D: Loss of distal pulses and capillary refill

explanation: As a circumferential burn swells, it acts like a tourniquet, cutting off circulation inside. Losing pulse and slow refill means pressure is dangerously high!

question: In Vroom's Expectancy Theory, what does the term 'valence' mean?

options.A: The belief that effort leads to good performance
options.B: The physical effort required for a clinical task
options.C: The guarantee that a reward will be delivered
options.D: The value an individual places on a specific reward

explanation: Valence is simply how much you actually want or care about the reward being offered. If management offers a prize you don't care about, your valence is low!

question: Which of the following is NOT a material commonly used during breast ironing?

options.A: Sterilized surgical scalpels
options.B: Hot metal spatulas
options.C: Heavy wooden pestles
options.D: Heated grinding stones

explanation: Surgical tools are not used in this abusive traditional practice; instead, household items like stones and pestles are heated. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T17#GNS312_U1_T17_h3)

question: Even if a bandage or gown looks completely dry, why should you still treat it as an infection risk?

options.A: Dry materials attract more pests than wet materials
options.B: Many harmful bacteria and viruses survive on dry surfaces for a long time
options.C: Dry waste automatically turns back into liquid when touched
options.D: Dried blood explodes into microscopic aerosols easily

explanation: Exactly! Just because something has dried out doesn't mean the germs are dead. Many pathogens are tough survivors and can remain infectious for a long while.

question: A patient asks how to lower their risk of type 2 diabetes. What is the best starting advice a nurse can give?

options.A: Sleep for at least 12 hours every night without exercising
options.B: Eliminate all carbohydrates completely from every meal
options.C: Take a daily low-dose insulin injection to rest the pancreas
options.D: Adopt a diet high in fiber and increase daily physical activity

explanation: Spot on! Eating healthy fiber and staying active directly fights insulin resistance, which is the root cause of type 2 diabetes.

question: A head nurse gives a junior nurse more independence after watching her successfully master wound dressings. What leadership style is this?

options.A: Transactional leadership
options.B: Situational leadership
options.C: Trait leadership theory
options.D: Laissez-faire leadership

explanation: Well done! Situational leaders adapt their approach to fit the changing skill level and confidence of their team members.

question: Which amino acid do renal tubule cells break down to produce ammonia and help buffer acid?

options.A: Glucose
options.B: Sodium
options.C: Albumin
options.D: Glutamine

explanation: When facing long-term acid buildup, kidney cells break down the amino acid glutamine to make ammonia, which acts as a shield to catch extra acid.

question: A community nurse helps a stroke patient practice daily walking exercises to regain strength. Which component of comprehensive care does this represent?

options.A: Disease prevention
options.B: Rehabilitative care
options.C: Health promotion
options.D: Curative services

explanation: Helping a patient recover lost functions and achieve independence after an illness or injury falls directly under rehabilitative care. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h3)

question: What is the main job of anti-spasmodic drugs in the tummy?

options.A: To coat the stomach lining and prevent acid ulcers
options.B: To kill harmful bacteria causing stomach infections
options.C: To speed up the transit time of stool in the colon
options.D: To relax overactive smooth muscle and relieve cramps

explanation: Think of anti-spasmodics as a calming massage for your gut muscles. They help stop those painful, tight cramps when the tummy muscles are working into overdrive!

question: Why is community participation critical after a health plan has been created?

options.A: It prevents the local government from taxing the primary health center
options.B: It creates a sense of ownership so the community maintains the project
options.C: It ensures that health workers receive extra allowances from donors
options.D: It allows nurses to transfer all their daily workload to local volunteers

explanation: When communities participate in identifying and planning solutions, they protect and sustain the project long after external funding ends. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T6#GNS124_U3_T6_h6)

question: In critical care, why do we need constant monitoring alongside regular physical checks?

options.A: Doctors rarely visit the intensive care unit more than once a day
options.B: Physical assessments are completely useless in critical care
options.C: Hospital accreditation standards legally demand constant monitoring
options.D: They experience rapid and unpredictable physiological shifts

explanation: Critical care patients can change in a matter of minutes! Continuous monitoring helps you catch hidden trouble early before it becomes a bigger crisis.

question: What is the best way for a nursing team to share their successful hospital study with others?

options.A: Keeping the final report locked inside a private desk drawer
options.B: Presenting at a healthcare conference or publishing in a peer-reviewed journal
options.C: Posting raw data sheets on a public community notice board
options.D: Destroying all copies to protect hospital operational secrets

explanation: Good nursing knowledge is meant to be shared! Conferences and journals help spread great ideas so patient care improves everywhere.

question: A competitive long-distance runner goes through intense training, loses a lot of weight, and her periods stop. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Primary ovarian failure
options.B: Functional hypothalamic amenorrhoea
options.C: Imperforate hymen
options.D: Pituitary adenoma

explanation: High physical stress and low energy stores can temporarily put the brakes on the hypothalamus, pausing the monthly cycle.

question: Why is nurse advocacy so important when it comes to disability and public policies?

options.A: To help enforce equal rights, accessibility, and reduce societal stigma
options.B: To stop families from caring for relatives at home
options.C: To replace the work of legal professionals in courtrooms
options.D: To secure direct political appointments for hospital administrators

explanation: You are a voice for your patients! Advocating for good policies ensures that people living with disabilities get fair treatment, access, and respect everywhere.

question: Which of these is a major warning sign of severe dehydration in a sick child?

options.A: Flushed skin that feels hot to the touch
options.B: An unusually loud and constant cry
options.C: Swelling in both lower legs and feet
options.D: Lethargy or unconsciousness with sunken eyes

explanation: When a child is severely dehydrated, they lose so much fluid that they become very weak, drowsy, or even unconscious, with noticeably sunken eyes. This is an emergency!

question: Why is it so important for you as a nurse to understand how a community functions?

options.A: To prescribe medications without needing a doctor
options.B: To manage hospital financial budgets and staff salaries
options.C: To understand how daily living conditions affect people's health
options.D: To diagnose rare genetic diseases in hospital laboratories

explanation: Spot on! The environment and everyday resources around your patients shape their health just as much as any medicine you give them.

question: Why do droplet precautions only need a regular surgical mask instead of an N95?

options.A: Droplets are heavy, travel short distances, and do not linger in the air
options.B: Droplets evaporate instantly before reaching any healthcare worker
options.C: Droplets can only pass through skin pores, not through cloth
options.D: Surgical masks filter out microscopic floating particles better than N95s

explanation: Exactly! Large droplets quickly drop down rather than floating, so a simple surgical mask gives you all the protection you need for close care.

question: What is the standard temperature range for maintaining the cold chain in vaccine storage?

options.A: Plus 15 degrees Celsius to plus 25 degrees Celsius

options.C: Plus 37 degrees Celsius to plus 40 degrees Celsius
options.D: Minus 20 degrees Celsius to minus 10 degrees Celsius

explanation: Most standard vaccines must be kept refrigerated between +2°C and +8°C to prevent them from spoiling. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T4#GNS225_U2_T4_h6)

question: A patient diagnosed with a serious illness insists the lab made a mistake and they are completely fine. What defense mechanism is this?

options.A: Regression
options.B: Intellectualization
options.C: Denial
options.D: Sublimation

explanation: Denial is our mind's way of protecting us by refusing to accept a painful or scary truth until we are ready to process it. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T15#GNS123_U3_T15_h6)

question: Which finding is specifically linked to Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA) rather than HHS?

options.A: Fruity breath odor and Kussmaul respirations
options.B: Extreme dehydration with normal blood pH
options.C: Total absence of any urinary symptoms
options.D: Rapid weight gain due to water retention

question: What is the main job of angiotensin II in the body?

options.A: Stopping all fluid movement through the capillary walls
options.B: Dilating peripheral blood vessels to lower heart rate
options.C: Constricting blood vessels to raise blood pressure
options.D: Increasing the heart's pumping speed without changing vessel size

explanation: Think of angiotensin II as a quick-fix squeeze: it tightens up your blood vessels so your blood pressure goes right back up when circulation drops.

question: Why is food safety such a big priority for community health nurses?

options.A: It directly reduces preventable gastrointestinal infections
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for community health clinics
options.C: It is the only way to treat chronic medical conditions
options.D: It stops all forms of malnutrition instantly

explanation: Spot on! When we teach and practice good food safety, we cut down massively on those painful, preventable stomach infections that bring patients into our clinics.

question: What are the three main tiers of the Nigerian health system?

options.A: Local, state, and federal hospitals
options.B: Community, general, and teaching units
options.C: Primary, secondary, and tertiary care
options.D: Private, public, and missionary clinics

explanation: Spot on! Nigeria's health system is broken into three simple levels (primary, secondary, and tertiary) to make sure healthcare reaches everyone from local villages to big cities.

question: Why do researchers process raw data in nursing studies?

options.A: To hide patient names to protect privacy
options.B: To increase the total number of study participants
options.C: To turn raw information into a structured, usable format
options.D: To write up the final hospital budget report

explanation: Great job thinking about research! Processing simply takes messy field notes or surveys and organizes them so you can actually study what they mean.

question: A nurse manager wants to compare monthly patient falls in the male ward versus the female ward for a whole year. Which graph should she use?

options.A: Pie chart

question: What physically causes the pulse wave that a nurse feels at an artery?

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard immediate action when caring for a patient in shock?

options.A: Providing high-flow oxygen
options.B: Administering a large oral meal
options.C: Establishing large-bore IV access
options.D: Applying warm blankets

question: What is the main reason a nurse uses the Braden Scale when a resident is admitted?

options.A: Measuring the severity of cognitive memory loss

question: Why is working with traditional and religious leaders so important when trying to stop early marriage?

options.A: They hold strong influence over community beliefs and practices

question: Which government body regulates health insurance in Nigeria?

options.D: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC)

question: How do communication breakdowns between hospital departments affect the DRF exemption process?

options.A: They force the federal government to send more medical equipment

options.C: They automatically increase the overall monthly revenue of the pharmacy

explanation: When departments fail to communicate well, vulnerable patients suffer dangerous delays while waiting for their paperwork to clear.

question: When a patient fasts, how does the body keep blood sugar from dropping too low?

options.A: The liver stops all metabolic activity until the next meal
options.B: The pancreas releases extra insulin to store extra sugar
options.C: The muscles absorb all available glucose to build up fat stores
options.D: The pancreas releases glucagon to tell the liver to release stored sugar

explanation: Think of glucagon as the body's natural backup alarm! When food isn't coming in, glucagon tells the liver to share its stored glucose to keep your energy stable.

question: As a caring nurse, why should you check in on the emotional wellbeing of a patient with endometriosis?

options.A: Chronic pain and potential fertility challenges can cause significant emotional distress
options.B: Hormonal medications prevent patients from feeling any physical pain
options.C: Mental health counseling can cure the physical growth of endometrial tissue
options.D: Anxiety and depression are the direct physical causes of retrograde menstruation

explanation: Living day in and day out with stubborn pain and worries about having kids can take a heavy emotional toll. Holistic nursing means supporting her mind too!

question: What is the medical name for a mouth fungal infection that shows creamy white patches?

options.A: Severe gingivitis
options.B: Chronic xerostomia
options.C: Acute periodontitis
options.D: Oral candidiasis

explanation: Candidiasis (often called thrush) happens when the Candida fungus grows out of control, which is common when a patient's immune system is low.

question: Which bone shape category does the patella ( kneecap) belong to?

options.A: Flat bone
options.B: Irregular bone

question: A mum in long labour has dry lips, dark urine, and a fast pulse. What is your best immediate nursing action?

options.A: Prepare the patient for immediate vaginal delivery
options.B: Encourage her to perform heavy physical exercises
options.C: Start an intravenous infusion to correct dehydration

question: What is the go-to medication used to speed up weak contractions during slow labour?

options.A: Nifedipine
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Magnesium sulfate
options.D: Ergometrine

explanation: Brilliant! Oxytocin mimics the body's natural contraction hormone to give the uterus the boost it needs.

question: At what tier of government is primary health care and public health nursing primarily managed in Nigeria?

options.A: Local government level
options.B: International embassy level
options.C: Global health organization level

question: Which substance serves as the main chemical building block for steroid hormones?

options.A: Tyrosine
options.B: Glucose
options.C: Nucleic acids
options.D: Cholesterol

explanation: Steroid hormones are made straight from cholesterol! Even though people often talk about cholesterol in a bad nutritional light, our bodies actually need it to build vital hormones.

question: Which medication history is crucial to check before doing a skin biopsy?

options.A: Anticoagulant or blood-thinning medications
options.B: Daily multivitamin and mineral supplements
options.C: Prescription oral birth control pills
options.D: Over-the-counter daily calcium tablets

question: Why is checking skin elasticity (turgor) alone not a reliable way to check for dehydration in an older adult?

options.A: Older adults always refuse to let nurses pinch their hands or arms.

question: Why should you teach deep breathing and coughing exercises along with giving an expectorant?

options.A: To slow down the heart rate during coughing fits

options.C: To help physically expel the mucus that the medication has loosened
options.D: To replace the need for drinking water during the daytime

question: What is the main job of memory cells in our immune system?

options.A: To fight off future exposures to the same pathogen much faster
options.B: To signal the brain when body temperature rises
options.C: To digest dead red blood cells in the spleen
options.D: To produce extra red blood cells during heavy bleeding

explanation: Think of memory cells as the immune system's security cameras—they remember past germs so the body can crush them instantly next time!

question: Why does the mother's uterine lining change into 'decidua' cells during early pregnancy?

options.A: To prevent the blastocyst from entering the myometrium
options.B: To close the cervical os tightly during early pregnancy
options.C: To provide early nourishment and support implantation
options.D: To stimulate immediate production of fetal red blood cells

explanation: Think of decidual cells as a welcoming host—they store helpful nutrients like fats and sugars to feed the tiny embryo before the full placenta takes over.

question: Why does injecting local numbing medicine directly into the middle of an inflamed abscess often not work very well?

options.A: The acidic environment of the pus neutralizes the local anesthetic
options.B: The nerve endings in the center are already permanently destroyed
options.C: The pus pressure pushes the medication back out the needle hole
options.D: The thick skin blocks the numbing medicine from spreading

explanation: Infected, pus-filled areas have an acidic chemistry that stops the numbing medicine from doing its job. That is why doctors usually numb the healthy skin around the edges instead!

question: What do we call those tiny, pinpoint red or purple spots caused by tiny bleeding vessels under the skin?

options.A: Petechiae
options.B: Pustules
options.C: Macules
options.D: Vesicles

explanation: Petechiae are those little pinpoint spots that show up when tiny blood vessels (capillaries) leak a bit of blood.

question: What is the normal, healthy pH range for human arterial blood?
explanation: Blood pH is tightly guarded between 7.35 and 7.45. Even a tiny shift outside this window can make a patient very sick, so the body works hard to protect it.

question: What is a great, simple first step a nurse can suggest to an overweight teenager looking to improve their diet?

options.A: Replace sugary sodas and packaged drinks with water.
options.B: Consume only liquid protein shakes until target weight is met.
options.C: Eliminate all carbohydrates from daily meals completely.
options.D: Fast for two full days every week to jumpstart weight loss.

explanation: Spot on! Swapping out sugary drinks for water cuts down on empty liquid calories easily without driving the teen toward unhealthy crash diets.

question: Why are audiovisual aids considered very powerful in nursing skills training?

options.A: They are always cheaper than printed books
options.B: They engage both the eyes and ears at the same time
options.C: They completely eliminate the need for a human instructor
options.D: They require no electricity to operate

explanation: Combining sight and sound mimics real-life clinical scenarios closely, improving retention and understanding for students. [learn more](GST321_U8_T4#GST321_U8_T4_h3)

question: A student gets severe eye strain and sleepiness during afternoon lectures in a room with no windows. What is the most likely physical cause?

options.A: Inadequate lighting
options.B: Poor acoustic design
options.C: Uncomfortable desk ergonomics
options.D: High social anxiety

explanation: Bad lighting in windowless rooms forces your eyes to work much harder, directly causing strain and tiredness. Good lighting makes a huge difference!

question: The Thomas-Kilmann conflict model is built on which two main personal behaviors?

options.A: Speed and accuracy
options.B: Assertiveness and cooperativeness
options.C: Empathy and detachment
options.D: Aggression and passivity

explanation: This model simply looks at two things: how much you push for your own needs versus how much you try to help the other person.

question: Why are maternal complications during childbirth considered so dangerous?

options.A: They only occur in women with a known history of chronic illness
options.B: They are completely preventable with strict bed rest during pregnancy
options.C: They usually respond slowly to standard emergency medical treatments
options.D: They develop suddenly and can quickly become fatal without prompt care

explanation: Complications like severe bleeding can start out of nowhere. That is why quick action from a skilled nurse is such a lifesaver!

question: A woman with a history of Type III FGM comes in for labor. What should the nurse watch out for?

options.A: Total absence of uterine contractions throughout the first stage
options.B: Obstructed labor and severe scarring requiring careful evaluation
options.C: Spontaneous healing of the infibulated scar without intervention
options.D: Rapid and completely painless expulsion of the placenta

explanation: That thick scar tissue blocks the normal stretching of the birth canal, often causing obstructed labor that needs careful handling. Clinical nursing in action!

question: Why do we use synthetic swab tips (like dacron) instead of regular cotton?

options.A: Synthetic swabs change color to indicate a positive infection
options.B: Cotton can inhibit certain laboratory tests and microbial growth
options.C: Synthetic tips are significantly cheaper to purchase in bulk
options.D: Cotton fibers dissolve completely when exposed to body fluids

explanation: Regular cotton can actually trap or stop germs from growing properly in the lab, so synthetic swabs give us much more reliable test results.

question: Roughly how long is a typical research report abstract?

options.A: 10 to 50 words
options.B: Exactly 5,000 words
options.C: 500 to 1,000 words
options.D: 150 to 250 words

explanation: An abstract is a short, sweet summary—usually just a couple of hundred words to give readers a quick preview.

question: A nurse discovers that a struggling patient in the ward cannot buy their prescribed antibiotics. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Advocate for the patient by contacting the social welfare unit for an exemption
options.B: Reprimand the patient for coming to the hospital without money
options.C: Ignore the situation because financial matters are outside nursing duties
options.D: Discharge the patient immediately from the hospital ward

explanation: You nailed it! As patient advocates, nurses bridge the gap by connecting vulnerable patients with social welfare so they can get their meds without delay.

question: A woman's last menstrual period began on January 1st. Using Naegele's rule, what is her estimated date of delivery (EDD)?

options.A: September 15th
options.B: November 5th
options.C: October 8th
options.D: December 25th

explanation: Easy trick: add 7 days to the first day of the last period, then subtract 3 months. Jan 1st + 7 days = Jan 8th, minus 3 months = October 8th!

question: Which clinical finding is an early indicator of hypovolemic shock?

options.A: Rapid and weak pulse
options.B: Warm and flushed skin color
options.C: Slow and bounding pulse
options.D: High and stable blood pressure

explanation: As blood volume drops, the heart beats faster to try and maintain adequate cardiac output and perfusion, resulting in a rapid, weak pulse. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T8#GNS112_U7_T8_h5)

question: What is the main tool used by nurses during labor to track progress and detect complications early?

options.A: Glucometer
options.B: Partograph
options.C: Otoscope
options.D: Sphygmomanometer

explanation: The partograph is a graphic record of labor used to monitor maternal and fetal well-being and flag prolonged labor. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h4)

question: What is a major advantage of decentralising decisions down to frontline ward managers?

options.A: Complete standardisation of every hospital procedure
options.B: Faster response times to daily operational challenges on the ward
options.C: Lower salaries for all categories of nursing staff
options.D: Elimination of all policies set by top hospital administration

explanation: You got it! Letting ward leaders solve local problems on the spot means they don't have to wait around for approval from distant executives.

question: Which two organs get a much-needed rest when you lower dietary fat?

options.A: Kidneys and urinary bladder
options.B: Pancreas and gallbladder
options.C: Spleen and large intestine
options.D: Thyroid and parathyroid glands

explanation: Great thinking! The pancreas and gallbladder work hard to break down fats, so cutting back gives them time to rest and heal.

question: Which health issue is closely linked to heavy metal exposure from bad toxic waste disposal?

options.A: Neurological damage
options.B: Seasonal allergies
options.C: Vision improvement
options.D: Muscle hypertrophy

explanation: That's correct! Toxic metals like lead and mercury attack the nervous system, leading to serious brain and developmental issues.

question: What does the principle of equity mean in public health?

options.A: Fair distribution of health resources to close gaps between different groups
options.B: Giving every single hospital the exact same amount of cash
options.C: Providing identical medical treatments to every patient regardless of age
options.D: Ensuring doctors earn the same salary as community health workers

explanation: Equity means giving fair opportunities and resources based on need so that everyone has a fair chance at good health, especially vulnerable populations. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h2)

question: What direction should you teach a new mother to clean her perineal area?

options.A: In a circular scrubbing motion
options.B: From front to back
options.C: From back to front
options.D: From side to side

explanation: Always front to back! This simple habit stops germs from the anal area from spreading to the healing vaginal and urinary openings.

question: Why is scolding or shouting at a returning defaulter a risky practice for a nurse?

options.A: It discourages the client from ever seeking care at that facility again
options.B: It violates international trade agreements
options.C: It instantly invalidates the chemical composition of oral pills
options.D: It causes immediate physical injury to the client's skin

explanation: Nobody wants to walk back into a place where they'll be judged. A welcoming attitude keeps our clinic doors open to those who need us most.

question: Which task can a registered nurse safely delegate to a nursing assistant?

options.A: Measuring routine vital signs on a stable patient
options.B: Performing a clinical assessment on a deteriorating patient
options.C: Administering a complex intravenous chemotherapy drug
options.D: Formulating the initial nursing care plan on admission

explanation: Routine, stable tasks like vital sign checks can be delegated to trained assistive personnel, unlike clinical assessment and care planning. [learn more](GST321_U1_T13#GST321_U1_T13_h6)

question: Which common side effect is often linked to ACE inhibitors like lisinopril?

options.A: A persistent dry cough
options.B: Extreme darkening of the urine
options.C: Severe yellowing of the eyes
options.D: Uncontrollable muscle twitching

explanation: You nailed it! ACE inhibitors can cause a buildup in the lungs that leads to a nagging, dry cough for some patients.

question: Which temporary foetal structure turns into the ligamentum arteriosum after birth?

options.A: Umbilical vein
options.B: Ductus venosus
options.C: Ductus arteriosus
options.D: Foramen ovale

explanation: Spot on! Once the ductus arteriosus finishes its job and seals up with high oxygen levels, it turns into a sturdy little ligament called the ligamentum arteriosum. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h7)

question: Why is keeping accurate, neat records so vital before you send off a referral?

options.A: It prevents the patient from visiting traditional birth attendants
options.B: It is required to qualify the clinic for international financial grants
options.C: It provides legal protection and proves what interventions were performed
options.D: It allows the nurse to charge extra consultation fees

explanation: You nailed it. Good notes protect you professionally by showing clear evidence of how you assessed, stabilized, and handed over the patient.

question: Which agency is primarily responsible for regulating medications in Nigeria?

options.A: NAFDAC
options.B: FMOH
options.C: NMNC
options.D: WHO

explanation: NAFDAC is our national watchdog ensuring that every drug distributed in Nigeria is safe and genuine. You'll see their stamp on almost every medication package!

question: Why do we wait to find out the exact name of the poison instead of panicking right away?

options.A: Laboratory tests are always inaccurate in the first hour
options.B: Immediate life threats must be managed to prevent death
options.C: Hospital policy forbids asking family members about pill bottles
options.D: The poison usually breaks down and cannot be identified later

explanation: Spot on! If a patient's airway is blocked or their heart stops, knowing the chemical name of the poison won't save them. We stabilize life first, investigate second.

question: What is a good alternative for severe hot flashes if a patient cannot take hormone therapy?

options.A: High-dose systemic testosterone injections
options.B: Strict fluid restriction during the evening hours
options.C: Low-dose non-hormonal neuromodulators like select SSRIs
options.D: Immediate surgical removal of the adrenal glands

explanation: Certain non-hormonal medications help calm the brain's thermostat to relieve hot flashes safely when hormones aren't an option.

question: What should you check or do first when a patient is brought in with a suspected poisoning?

options.A: Drawing blood for toxicology screening
options.B: Identifying the specific poison
options.C: Administering activated charcoal immediately
options.D: Stabilizing the airway, breathing, and circulation

explanation: Great nursing rule to keep in mind! ABC comes before anything else in an emergency. We have to make sure our patient is breathing and has a steady heartbeat before we worry about testing or finding out what they swallowed.

question: A patient comes in with a suspected blood clot in their leg vein (deep vein thrombosis). What scan will the doctor likely order?

options.A: Renal B-Mode ultrasound
options.B: Pelvic M-Mode ultrasound
options.C: Cardiac echocardiogram
options.D: Vascular Doppler ultrasound

explanation: A vascular Doppler scan is specifically designed to peek inside blood vessels and catch clots early.

question: You finish helping a patient and notice visible blood on your bare hands. What is your immediate next step?

options.A: Wash hands thoroughly with soap and running water
options.B: Apply an alcohol-based hand rub and rub briskly
options.C: Put on clean gloves without washing the hands
options.D: Wipe the hands clean with a dry paper towel

explanation: Right! When hands are visibly soiled with blood or body fluids, soap and water are a must because alcohol rubs can't wash away the physical dirt.

question: A young female patient is treated for chlamydia. What crucial step must you take as a nurse to prevent the infection from coming back?

options.A: Advise her to avoid all physical exercise for six months
options.B: Schedule immediate surgical removal of the fallopian tubes
options.C: Ensure her sexual partners are also evaluated and treated
options.D: Prescribe long-term daily hormonal contraceptive pills

explanation: You nailed it! Treating partners stops the back-and-forth spread of infection and keeps your patient safe from repeated pelvic inflammation. Great clinical thinking!

question: A nurse wants to understand the daily emotional experiences of mothers caring for children with chronic kidney disease. Which approach is best?

options.A: Qualitative phenomenology
options.B: Epidemiological survey
options.C: Quantitative correlational
options.D: Experimental clinical trial

explanation: Phenomenology sounds like a big word, but it just means studying the 'lived experience' of people going through a specific life event. Perfect for capturing their real stories!

question: What is the main purpose of post-administration monitoring?

options.A: To calculate the nurse's daily productivity score
options.B: To check if the drug is working and watch for adverse reactions
options.C: To ensure the patient finishes their hospital meal on time
options.D: To clean up the medication trolley and return supplies

explanation: Monitoring helps nurses catch unexpected side effects early and evaluate whether the therapeutic goal was achieved. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T2#GNS125_U4_T2_h7)

question: Why is physical therapy for a stroke survivor considered tertiary prevention?

options.A: It limits disability and helps restore function after the damage has happened
options.B: It screens the general population for hidden high blood pressure
options.C: It stops the stroke from occurring in a healthy person
options.D: It eliminates environmental toxins that cause blood vessel disease

explanation: Exactly! Rehabilitation is all about helping patients regain independence and manage existing health challenges.

question: What actually happens during a heart attack (myocardial infarction)?

options.A: The heart beats too slowly to pump blood to the brain.
options.B: A blood clot completely blocks a coronary artery, causing tissue death.
options.C: Blood leaks backward through the mitral valve into the lung.
options.D: The coronary sinus fails to empty blood into the right atrium.

explanation: You nailed it! When a coronary artery is completely blocked, the heart muscle cells downstream get starved of oxygen and start to die.

question: What is maceration in the context of skin care?

options.A: Skin becoming completely numb to all touch
options.B: Skin turning completely black from cold temperatures
options.C: Skin growing extra thick layers like a hard shell
options.D: Skin becoming soft and broken down from too much moisture

explanation: Maceration happens when moisture stays on the skin too long, making the tissue weak and prone to damage. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h8)

question: What does a "high-risk labour" mean for a mother and her baby?

options.A: A guarantee that a cesarean section is legally required
options.B: A pregnancy that requires no special medical supervision
options.C: An absolute certainty that the baby will be born premature
options.D: A greater chance of illness or death during childbirth

explanation: You've got this! High-risk labour just means there's an increased chance of complications for either mum or baby, so we need to keep our eyes open and stay extra vigilant.

question: What is the primary purpose of performing an ophthalmoscopy?

options.A: To check the outer muscles that move the eyeball around
options.B: To view the internal structures of the back of the eye
options.C: To test the patient for clear distance and reading vision
options.D: To measure the exact fluid pressure inside the eyeball

explanation: Ophthalmoscopy specifically directs light through the pupil to examine the internal fundus, which includes the retina and optic disc. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T8#GNS221_U2_T8_h1)

question: A patient taking a new blood pressure medication suddenly feels very dizzy and lightheaded when standing up. What is the most appropriate immediate nursing action?

options.A: Tell the patient to run in place to improve blood circulation
options.B: Administer a stimulant medication to raise the blood pressure
options.C: Check the patient's blood pressure and pulse immediately
options.D: Wait until the next scheduled clinic visit to report the finding

explanation: Dizziness after starting a new blood pressure drug points to orthostatic hypotension, requiring a check of vital signs. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h6)
